title: DyGen: Learning from Noisy Labels via Dynamics-Enhanced Generative Modeling

problem.claim: Learning from noisy labels is challenging, and language models fine-tuned with noisy labels can overfit label noise and suffer decreased performance.

gap.claim: Methods based on static input features provide limited information about true label distributions and can produce biased or incorrect predictions.

contributions.claim: DyGen uses dynamic patterns in the embedding space during language-model fine-tuning to improve noisy-label predictions.

DyGen applies variational auto-encoding to infer posterior distributions of true labels from noisy labels and training dynamics, with co-regularization to reduce the impact of potentially noisy labels and priors.

author_reported_evidence.claim: DyGen reports average accuracy improvements of 3.10% on two synthetic-noise datasets and 1.48% on three real-world-noise datasets compared with the previous state of the art.
The authors report that extensive experiments and analyses show the effectiveness of each DyGen component.
The authors report that code is available on GitHub for reproducibility.

narrative_sequence.summary: Noisy labels create a broad learning challenge and can cause language models to overfit label noise.
Static-feature denoising methods may lack information about true label distributions and produce biased or incorrect predictions.
DyGen models noisy-label prediction using fine-tuning dynamics, variational inference, and co-regularization.
The authors report accuracy gains across synthetic and real-world noise datasets and component-effectiveness analyses.
Code is reported as available on GitHub.

source_observation.claim: Static input features may provide limited information about true label distributions, while training dynamics contain additional signals used by DyGen.

interpretation.claim: For noisy-label problems, temporal or process-level representations may complement static features when estimating latent label structure.

application.claim: Consider incorporating training dynamics into generative or probabilistic noisy-label models when static-feature denoising is insufficient.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when dynamics-based modeling is preferable across tasks, noise processes, or model architectures.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, noise rates, or statistical significance of the reported improvements.
The abstract does not describe the training-dynamics features, model architecture details, or ablation results.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported results or code availability.
